## Why

Applying a filter is a signal. Exporting a file that keeps the filter is the win. We currently measure the signal and not the win, and the few numbers we do have describe ourselves.

Measured 25 Aug 2026 in the example app, last 90 days:

|  | Total | Users |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `demo_filter_applied` | 81 | 12 |
| `demo_export` | 4,210 | 305 |

Applies by filter: `sketch-outline` 52, `color-wash` 17, `grain-filter` 9, `soft-shadow` 3, `mirror-tile` 0.

The events themselves are fine. They fire, they arrive, and their properties are correct — checked against the raw event stream, not inferred from the code. The volume is small because the filters are held to staff accounts until launch. Twelve of those users are us.

## How the work splits

Launch is the hinge. Before it, everything that can be proved or prepared without an audience. After it, the analysis that only becomes possible once the filters are open to everyone.

Doing the preparation now means launch starts with instrumentation already trusted, instead of a month spent debugging telemetry while the numbers finally matter.

## Children

1. Declare the filter events in the tracking plan
2. Chart: filter speed and failure rate
3. Chart: repeat use and adoption
4. Chart: filtered share of exports (after launch)

[WEB-3179](https://linear.app/example/issue/WEB-3179/tag-exports-that-carry-a-filter) is the code change the fourth one depends on: it tags each export that carries a filter, so the headline metric becomes computable at all. It is open and waiting on review.

## Two caveats for anyone reading these charts

Exclude sample projects on every chart. Sample projects are seeded content.

A pre-launch baseline is staff behaviour, not customer behaviour. Do not carry one across the launch line as a comparison.

## Settle before launch, not after

What an acceptable filtered-export rate actually looks like. A number chosen after seeing the first week tends to be the number the first week produced.
